item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it exposes the exact required Upload signature, uses multipartbody.NewFile, preserves FilesOption semantics, and tests multipart encoding plus retry from an os.File. A violates several explicit API and scope requirements.","reasons":["B’s Upload signature exactly matches `Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption) (*File, error)`; A substitutes `...UploadFileOption`.","B directly reuses `internal/multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content)`, while A adds unnecessary `NewFileWithFields` machinery.","A adds association options and arbitrary multipart fields despite the explicit prohibition on adding association fields.","A refactors generic request-body replay behavior and changes seekable-reader closing and Content-Length semantics, contrary to the instruction not to refactor unrelated request/retry machinery directly introduced by A’s upload design scope; B keeps retryability localized to file handling and adds Upload tests with a streamed source."],"risks_a":["Upload does not accept ordinary FilesOption values by contract; only newly introduced shared option types happen to overlap.","Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its request construction, response decoding, and error handling.","Adds multiple forbidden public APIs and changes existing option constructor return types, increasing compatibility and maintenance risk despite interface satisfaction in common calls and recorded compatibility gates; it also expands changelog and README around out-of-contract behavior."],"risks_b":["It changes Add from streaming to eagerly buffering every caller-provided body, violating the requirement to preserve Add behavior and potentially increasing memory use or blocking on long-lived readers.","Upload calls the new private `add` helper instead of routing through the existing public Add method, weakening the contract’s single-path requirement.","Visible tests do not cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures as explicitly requested."]}
